pairs.subject: candidate-ai-disclosure-and-explanation
pairs.evidence: app/status/[token]/StatusClient.tsx:397 The review right on the decision history is a sentence (en.json status.decisions.humanReviewNote: "Just reply to any message from the hiring team"), not a mechanism. Separately, the renderer falls back to a de-snaked kind name, hides decisions whose attribution is unknown, and shows the model's self-reported confidence.

techniques.evidence: app/status/[token]/StatusClient.tsx:397 The copy resolves to "You can request a human review of any decision at any time. Just reply to any message from the hiring team." That is the reply-to-any-message shape the technique calls a contact address. There is no control carrying the decision id, nothing routes it, and nothing seals the outcome.

app/status/[token]/StatusClient.tsx:349 The server allowlists kinds (CANDIDATE_VISIBLE_DECISION_KINDS, status-decisions.ts:89). The renderer still has the humanised-identifier fallback the technique forbids, and the comment at lines 186-188 says so deliberately. A kind admitted server-side without copy renders as its de-snaked enum name.

app/status/[token]/StatusClient.tsx:350 An unknown attribution renders no label at all, where the technique requires an explicit 'cannot determine'. Downgrade-not-upgrade (sealedActorAttribution) and the automated+person-approved two-fact rendering (lines 353-356) are realized.

app/status/[token]/StatusClient.tsx:389 The threshold pair and its sealed staleness caveat cross correctly (lines 370-371), and rubric dimensions are shown. But the verdict facts emit the AI scorer's own confidence percentage. The technique names a model's self-reported confidence as something not to emit.

app/status/[token]/page.tsx:22 The regime is resolved server-side, so there is no client-default first paint. But disclosureComplianceFor (compliance-disclosure.ts:45) returns DEFAULT_REGIME_ID when the lookup throws. AiDisclosure then renders regimeNote naming that regime's laws, so a failed lookup is treated as the home regime rather than as unknown.

app/status/[token]/StatusClient.tsx:419 This page has no what-we-hold inventory; that sits behind the /data link. The one held-data item it does show, the recording, is gated on its actual presence, which matches the technique's spirit.
